items.desc: The world’s youngest national leader makes his UN debut as Nepal seeks greater support for communities bearing the costs of climate disasters.

items.title: Congress to elect thousands of young faces to its ranks
items.desc: At least 13,483 people under 35 are guaranteed places in party committees from the ward to the central level, with more young members winning leadership posts through open competition.

items.title: Friendly rivalry turns fiery as Bista and Chaudhary headline debut Fusion Fight
items.desc: Tied 1-1 in career head-to-heads, Nepal’s top female Muay Thai fighters trade knockout threats ahead of their October 10 face-off.

items.title: What is a ‘super El Niño’ and how will it affect the weather?
items.desc: A potentially record-strength El Niño could drive extreme heat, floods and droughts worldwide, with major risks to crops, food security and public health.

items.title: Educationist Suresh Raj Sharma cremated with state honours
items.desc: Sharma helped build Kathmandu University into an autonomous institution with an international profile during more than two decades of leadership.

items.title: Biratnagar’s industrial engine slows. Can it regain its old shine?
items.desc: Once home to more than 600 factories and 100,000 direct jobs, Biratnagar’s industrial sector is struggling with weak demand, rising costs, cross-border competition and a lack of new investment. Regular cargo rail offers a glimmer of hope.

items.title: A diplomatic split screen as Trump and Xi meet
items.desc: Trump-Xi talks in Washington highlight questions over the UN’s influence amid financial strain and global conflicts.

items.title: Heavy rain prompts travel curbs, school closures across Nepal
items.desc: Authorities suspend night-time transport, close schools and urge people to postpone travel as heavy rainfall raises the risk of floods and landslides.

items.title: Narayanghat-Muglin road to shut overnight as rain raises landslide risk
items.desc: Chitwan authorities will halt all traffic from 8pm Thursday to 5am Friday as forecasters warn of heavy rain, floods and landslides across Nepal.

items.title: Nepal women’s kabaddi team seals Asian Games medal
items.desc: A 34-24 win over Sri Lanka takes Nepal into the semi-finals and assures the team at least a bronze medal.

items.title: What Nepal actually needs from global leaders in New York
items.desc: Former under-secretary-general of the UN argues Balendra Shah’s UNGA debut is a critical pulpit to demand climate justice, secure reconstruction aid and champion the fragile future of the world’s mountains.

items.title: Inside Kathmandu’s Kumari puja tradition
items.desc: Young Newar girls aged 2 to 8 take part in a traditional worship ritual at Hanuman Dhoka, where devotees seek blessings for peace, prosperity and protection.

items.title: Kane considers NFL kicking career after soccer
items.desc: England captain says the NFL is a more realistic option than golf, with a possible MLS move helping him make the transition.

items.title: Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal calls for climate action beyond commitments
items.desc: Khanal urges faster climate finance, stronger adaptation measures and greater support for countries facing the growing impacts of climate change.

items.title: Seven die of scrub typhus in one month in Salyan
items.desc: Fifty-four people tested positive in two days as confirmed cases rise to 114 in Darma Rural Municipality.

items.title: Sita Air aircraft tyre comes off during landing at Dolpa airport
items.desc: Thirteen passengers, including seven foreign nationals, were unharmed after the aircraft’s rear tyre came off on landing, blocking the runway and disrupting flights.

items.title: Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal seeks greater international support for Nepal’s recovery and climate resilience
items.desc: Khanal calls for more support for Nepal’s post-disaster recovery, climate-resilient infrastructure, disaster preparedness and financing for climate-vulnerable countries.

items.title: RSP’s repeated attacks on the judiciary threaten to undermine its independence
items.desc: The court’s rulings can be questioned, but expecting the judiciary to rule in the government’s favour goes against the principle of separation of powers.

items.title: How Nepal can lead the global climate charge at UNGA 81 and beyond
items.desc: From building global alliances at UNGA 81 to rallying vulnerable nations for COP31, former assistant secretary-general of the UN outlines a roadmap for urgent climate action and financing.

items.title: Rasuwa flash floods recede, health risks loom
items.desc: Reliable systems for providing safe drinking water, sustained hygiene promotion and community awareness programmes are urgently needed.

items.title: At UN, Prime Minister Balendra Shah to make Nepal’s case for climate justice
items.desc: Shah will cite the Bhotekoshi flood devastation and ask wealthy nations to provide more money, technology and support for reconstruction.

items.title: Expressway deadline extended for third time as project nears a decade with half the work unfinished
items.desc: The 70.97-kilometre national project, being constructed by the Nepali Army, is progressing slowly, leading to significant cost overruns.

items.title: PM Shah arrives in New York to lead Nepal’s UN delegation
items.desc: The prime minister is scheduled to meet UN Secretary-General António Guterres and attend a reception hosted by Nepal’s mission.

items.title: NEA working on winter power management
items.desc: Officials say there won’t be load-shedding this winter despite flood damage to hydropower infrastructure along Trishuli corridor.

items.title: From a rented room in Bauddha to the Asian Games podium
items.desc: Karateka Tenzing Sherpa, 23, overcomes a difficult start, a semifinal defeat and his short temper to dominate Laos’s Xayasan Vatthana and secure Nepal’s first medal of the 20th Asian Games.

items.title: Avoid long-distance travel from Friday to Sunday, suspend Himalayan treks: Met office
items.desc: Weather experts urge trekkers already in the mountains to return to safer, lower elevations and ask the public to take precautions.

items.title: Kathmandu University founding vice-chancellor Suresh Raj Sharma dies
items.desc: Sharma, 86, played a key role in the development of technical and higher education in Nepal.

items.title: Flydubai begins regular international flights from Pokhara
items.desc: The daily Dubai-Pokhara service opens a new international air link for the tourism hub, with passengers also able to connect to more than 250 cities through Dubai.

items.title: BP Highway to close at night in Kavrepalanchok from September 24 to 28 amid flood risk
items.desc: Authorities will stop vehicles from using the highway from 5 pm to 5 am, while the weather office has urged people to postpone long-distance travel from September 25 to 27.

items.title: AI leaders to brief UN amid warnings the technology could slip beyond human control
items.desc: Altman plans to urge world leaders to adopt benchmarks for measuring AI capabilities and ​assessing the safeguards companies put in place as they develop the technology, an OpenAI executive told reporters on Tuesday.
